newsitem.title: USA: Foreign crudes into U.S. Gulf quiet to start week.
newsitem.headline: Foreign crudes into U.S. Gulf quiet to start week.

text.p: Foreign crude offerings into the U.S. Gulf continued quiet on Monday, following a sluggish Friday session to end a tumultuous week, traders said.
"I was trying to get some Oriente into the West Coast, but there was nothing going today at all in any market," said a foreign cash broker.
Trade was extremely light in London as well, with Brent paper and spot market firming slightly.
A cargo of May 4-6 brent was picked-up at June Brent -37 cents, with a second cargo bought at a dated related price.
Paper Brent values slipped slighty in London, but in late U.S. trade a U.K. major unloaded a full cargo to a Wall Street broker 4 cts above the IPE settle at $18.30, traders said.
Offerings into the U.S. focused on West African barrels, with a U.S. major said to be shopping Nigerian Qua Iboe for middle-June at dated Brent plus 40-45 cts.

Continued ethnic fighting has aided Nigerian values in the past few sessions. Royal Dutch/Shell, however, announced it had resumed normal Forcados production Monday morning after sealing a deal with local communities to restart closed flow stations.
On Friday, Shell said it had cut Forcados production 20 percent and declared force majeure with liftings from April 29 expected delayed two to three days.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing-Brent spreads evened out to around $1.55 late Monday, around the same levels as seen on Friday.
